prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

The goal of this paper is to construct invariant dynamical objects for a (not necessarily invertible) smooth self map of a compact manifold. We prove a result that takes advantage of differences in rates of expansion in the terms of a sheaf cohomological long exact sequence to create unique lifts of finite dimensional invariant subspaces of one term of the sequence to invariant subspaces of the preceding term. This allows us to take invariant cohomological classes and under the right circumstances construct unique currents of a given type, including unique measures of a given type, that represent those classes and are invariant under pullback. A dynamically interesting self map may have a plethora of invariant measures, so the uniquess of the constructed currents is important. It means that if local growth is not too big compared to the growth rate of the cohomological class then the expanding cohomological class gives sufficient "marching orders" to the system to prohibit the formation of any other such invariant current of the same type (say from some local dynamical subsystem). Because we use subsheaves of the sheaf of currents we give conditions under which a subsheaf will have the same cohomology as the sheaf containing it. Using a smoothing argument this allows us to show that the sheaf cohomology of the currents under consideration can be canonically identified with the deRham cohomology groups. Our main theorem can be applied in both the smooth and holomorphic setting.

outputs.L1:
The goal of this paper is to construct invariant dynamical objects for a smooth self-map of a compact manifold, not necessarily invertible. We prove a result that exploits differences in expansion rates among the terms of a long exact sequence in sheaf cohomology to produce unique lifts of finite-dimensional invariant subspaces of one term to invariant subspaces of the preceding term. Under suitable conditions, this enables us to associate invariant cohomology classes with unique currents of a prescribed type—including unique measures of a prescribed type—that represent those classes and are invariant under pullback.

A dynamically interesting self-map may admit a plethora of invariant measures, making the uniqueness of the currents constructed here particularly significant. Specifically, if local growth is not too large relative to the growth rate of a cohomology class, then the expanding class provides sufficient “marching orders” to preclude the formation of any other invariant current of the same type, including one arising from a local dynamical subsystem.

Because our approach uses subsheaves of the sheaf of currents, we establish conditions under which a subsheaf has the same cohomology as the ambient sheaf. Combined with a smoothing argument, these conditions allow us to show that the sheaf cohomology of the currents under consideration can be canonically identified with the de Rham cohomology groups. Our main theorem applies in both the smooth and holomorphic settings.
outputs.L2:
This paper aims to construct invariant dynamical objects for a smooth self-map of a compact manifold, without assuming that the map is invertible. We establish a result that exploits disparities among expansion rates in the terms of a long exact sequence in sheaf cohomology. These disparities yield unique lifts of finite-dimensional invariant subspaces from one term of the sequence to invariant subspaces in the preceding term.

Consequently, under suitable hypotheses, invariant cohomology classes can be represented by uniquely determined currents of a prescribed type—including measures of a specified kind—that remain invariant under pullback. Since a dynamically significant self-map may admit many invariant measures, the uniqueness of these currents is essential. More precisely, when local growth is sufficiently small relative to the growth rate of the cohomology class, the expanding class imposes enough dynamical constraints to rule out any other invariant current of the same type, including one arising from a local dynamical subsystem.

Because our approach uses subsheaves of the sheaf of currents, we provide criteria ensuring that such a subsheaf has the same cohomology as its ambient sheaf. A smoothing argument then gives a canonical identification between the sheaf cohomology of the currents under consideration and the de Rham cohomology groups. The principal theorem applies in both smooth and holomorphic contexts.
outputs.L3:
The paper develops a general framework for constructing invariant dynamical objects associated with smooth self-maps of compact manifolds, without requiring the maps to be invertible. Its central mechanism is based on a long exact sequence in sheaf cohomology. When a finite-dimensional invariant subspace in one term expands at a rate that is sufficiently different from the growth rate in the preceding term, the subspace admits a unique invariant lift to that preceding term. Thus, a spectral gap between dynamical expansion rates becomes a tool for producing canonical invariant representatives.

Applied to cohomology classes, this principle shows that, under appropriate hypotheses, invariant classes determine unique pullback-invariant currents representing them. These currents may include measures as a special case. The key requirement is that local growth—measuring the possible proliferation or amplification of representatives at small scales—remain sufficiently weak compared with the expansion rate of the induced action on cohomology. This separation prevents the existence of distinct invariant currents of the same type representing the same class, thereby ensuring uniqueness.

A smoothing argument further shows that the sheaf cohomology used in the construction is canonically identified with de Rham cohomology. Consequently, the invariant currents produced by the abstract sheaf-theoretic method represent ordinary de Rham classes and do not depend on auxiliary choices. The resulting main theorem therefore provides a unified construction of canonical invariant currents and measures in both the smooth and holomorphic settings, including for noninvertible dynamical systems.
outputs.L4:
The paper develops a general sheaf-cohomological framework for constructing invariant dynamical objects associated with smooth self-maps of compact manifolds. The maps under consideration need not be invertible, so standard arguments based on backward iteration or invariant foliations are not always available. Instead, the method begins with the action induced by pullback on a finite-dimensional subspace of cohomology and seeks to realize that algebraic action on a larger space of geometric objects, such as differential forms, currents, or measures.

The central problem is a lifting problem. A cohomology class may be invariant, or more generally may transform under pullback by a prescribed linear operator, but a representative of that class need not satisfy the same relation exactly. The discrepancy between the pullback of a representative and the desired invariant representative is cohomologically trivial and can therefore be treated as an error term. By organizing representatives and error terms into appropriate sheaves and quotient spaces, the paper turns the construction of an invariant current into the problem of uniquely lifting a finite-dimensional invariant cohomology subspace through a sequence of sheaf-theoretic extensions.

The key hypothesis is a separation between two rates of growth. On the one hand, pullback acts on the selected cohomology subspace with a definite expansion rate. On the other hand, pullback also produces local growth in the ambient sheaves of forms, distributions, or currents. If the expansion on cohomology dominates this local growth, normalized pullbacks contract the cohomologically trivial errors. Iterating the pullback then yields a convergent correction procedure. Starting with any representative of the chosen class, one repeatedly pulls it back and renormalizes according to the cohomological action; the accumulated exact or locally trivial terms converge, producing a current that transforms exactly as prescribed.

This domination condition also gives uniqueness. If two invariant currents represent the same cohomology class, their difference lies in the cohomologically trivial part of the ambient space. The normalized pullback contracts that difference because its local growth is smaller than the expansion rate of the cohomological class. Consequently, the difference must vanish. Thus the construction does more than prove the existence of an invariant representative: it selects a canonical current determined by the dynamics and the chosen cohomology class.

In the simplest one-dimensional situation, if a class \(c\) satisfies
\[
f^{*}c=\lambda c,
\]
the method produces a representative \(T\) satisfying
\[
f^{*}T=\lambda T,
\qquad [T]=c.
\]
For a higher-dimensional invariant subspace, the scalar \(\lambda\) is replaced by the linear action of \(f^{*}\) on that subspace, and the resulting family of currents realizes the same finite-dimensional representation. When the degree and positivity properties are appropriate, these currents can be interpreted as invariant or eigenmeasures. In this way, an expanding cohomological direction is converted into a genuine dynamical object on the manifold.

A significant technical component of the paper is the comparison between the sheaf-theoretic construction and ordinary de Rham cohomology. Spaces of currents are large enough to contain limits of normalized pullbacks, but their cohomology must still be identified with the familiar topological cohomology of the manifold. Smoothing operators provide this bridge. They approximate currents by smooth differential forms while controlling the difference by exact terms, showing that the relevant complexes of generalized forms and currents compute the same cohomology as the smooth de Rham complex. This permits the lifting argument to be carried out in flexible distributional spaces without losing the geometric meaning of the original cohomology classes.

The framework is deliberately formulated so that it applies beyond a single regularity category. In smooth dynamics, it yields invariant currents and measures for noninvertible maps whenever the required spectral domination is available. In holomorphic dynamics, the same mechanism can be adapted to complexes of currents compatible with the complex structure, including currents of prescribed bidegree and, when additional positivity arguments apply, positive closed currents. The method therefore unifies constructions that might otherwise appear to depend on separate analytic techniques.

Conceptually, the main contribution is to isolate a broad principle: sufficiently rapid expansion in cohomology forces the existence of a unique geometric representative whose transformation law exactly matches the cohomological one. Sheaf cohomology records the obstruction to choosing such representatives, growth estimates control the local errors, and smoothing identifies the resulting classes with de Rham cohomology. Together, these ingredients provide a robust method for passing from finite-dimensional algebraic information about the pullback action to canonical invariant currents or measures that describe the underlying dynamics.

counterfactuals.output: We develop a cohomological method for constructing invariant currents and measures for smooth, possibly noninvertible, self-maps of compact manifolds. The approach combines sheaf-theoretic resolutions of locally constant coefficients with quantitative estimates on the induced action on differential forms and currents. Under a spectral-gap hypothesis separating the growth of a distinguished cohomology class from the relevant geometric expansion rates, normalized iterates converge, in an appropriate weak topology, to a canonical invariant current representing that class. Positivity criteria then promote these currents to finite invariant measures. The construction does not require global inverse branches and therefore applies naturally to branched and noninvertible dynamics. We establish existence, cohomological uniqueness, and stability under perturbation, and relate the resulting invariant objects to the dominant action on sheaf cohomology. This provides a unified framework connecting topological growth, differential expansion, and invariant distributions in smooth dynamics.

counterfactuals.output: A central problem in complex dynamics is to determine when the cohomological action of a self-map selects a canonical invariant current. Let \(f\colon X\to X\) be a dominant self-map of a compact Kähler manifold, and suppose that a nef or pseudoeffective class \(\alpha\in H^{1,1}(X,\mathbf R)\) is expanding, in the sense that \(f^{*}\alpha=\lambda\alpha\) for some \(\lambda>1\). Normalized pullbacks \(\lambda^{-n}(f^{n})^{*}\theta\) of a representative \(\theta\in\alpha\) then naturally lead to a positive closed current \(T_{\alpha}\) satisfying \(f^{*}T_{\alpha}=\lambda T_{\alpha}\). The main issue is uniqueness, since distinct currents in the same class may differ by singular potentials. If the local dynamical growth—measured, for example, by multiplicities, local degrees, or the amplification of singularities along backward orbits—is uniformly smaller than the cohomological expansion rate \(\lambda\), these potential differences are contracted under normalized pullback. Consequently, no nontrivial singular correction can remain invariant, and the expanding class \(\alpha\) uniquely determines the pullback-invariant current \(T_{\alpha}\).

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain, in technical mathematical language, a theorem that constructs unique invariant representatives of cohomology classes via differences in expansion rates, including the role of subsheaves of currents, smoothing, and de Rham cohomology.
counterfactuals.output:
### Spectral-gap theorem for invariant current representatives

Let \(M\) be a compact smooth manifold and \(f\colon M\to M\) a \(C^\infty\) diffeomorphism. Let  
\[
(\mathscr C^\bullet,d)
\]
be a complex of subsheaves of the sheaves of currents on \(M\), stable under pullback \(f^*\). Assume:

1. **Fine resolution.** The sequence
   \[
   0\longrightarrow \mathbb R_M
   \longrightarrow \mathscr C^0
   \xrightarrow d \mathscr C^1
   \xrightarrow d\cdots
   \]
   is locally exact and the sheaves \(\mathscr C^q\) are fine.

2. **Smoothing homotopy.** There are smoothing operators
   \[
   R_\varepsilon\colon \mathscr C^q(M)\to \Omega^q(M)
   \]
   and degree \(-1\) operators \(A_\varepsilon\) such that
   \[
   I-R_\varepsilon=dA_\varepsilon+A_\varepsilon d.
   \]
   The operators preserve the relevant current spaces and are compatible with their topology.

3. **Expansion-rate gap.** In degree \(q\), let
   \[
   E^q=d\mathscr C^{q-1}(M)
   \]
   denote the space of exact currents. Suppose the growth of \(f^*\) on \(E^q\) is bounded by a rate \(\rho_q\), in the sense that, in a suitable Banach or locally convex realization,
   \[
   \|(f^*)^n|_{E^q}\|\le C_\epsilon(\rho_q+\epsilon)^n.
   \]
   Let \(\lambda\) be an eigenvalue of
   \[
   f^*\colon H^q_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;\mathbb C)\to
   H^q_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;\mathbb C)
   \]
   satisfying
   \[
   |\lambda|>\rho_q.
   \]

Then every cohomology class \(c\in H^q_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;\mathbb C)\) with
\[
f^*c=\lambda c
\]
has a unique representative \(T_c\in \mathscr C^q(M)\), unique within its cohomology class, such that
\[
dT_c=0,\qquad f^*T_c=\lambda T_c,\qquad [T_c]=c.
\]

Equivalently, \(T_c\) is invariant under the normalized pullback
\[
\lambda^{-1}f^*T_c=T_c.
\]

## Construction

Choose a smooth closed form \(\alpha\) representing \(c\). Since \(c\) is a \(\lambda\)-eigenclass,
\[
\delta:=f^*\alpha-\lambda\alpha
\]
is exact. We seek an exact current \(e\in E^q\) such that
\[
T_c=\alpha+e
\]
satisfies \(f^*T_c=\lambda T_c\). This is equivalent to
\[
(\lambda-f^*)e=\delta.
\]

The expansion-rate inequality makes \(\lambda-f^*\) invertible on \(E^q\). Its inverse is represented by the convergent Neumann series
\[
(\lambda-f^*)^{-1}
=
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\lambda^{-n-1}(f^*)^n.
\]
Hence
\[
T_c
=
\alpha+
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}
\lambda^{-n-1}(f^*)^n
\bigl(f^*\alpha-\lambda\alpha\bigr).
\]
The series generally need not converge in \(C^\infty\), which is why one works in a suitably chosen subsheaf of currents or an anisotropic distribution space.

## Why uniqueness follows from the rate gap

If \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) are two equivariant representatives of the same class, then
\[
u=T_1-T_2\in E^q
\]
is exact and satisfies
\[
f^*u=\lambda u.
\]
But the growth bound on exact currents gives
\[
\|(f^*)^n u\|\lesssim \rho_q^n\|u\|,
\]
whereas equivariance gives
\[
(f^*)^n u=\lambda^n u.
\]
Since \(|\lambda|>\rho_q\), these two estimates are compatible only when \(u=0\). Thus \(T_1=T_2\).

## Role of smoothing and de Rham cohomology

The smoothing identity
\[
I-R_\varepsilon=dA_\varepsilon+A_\varepsilon d
\]
shows that every closed current in \(\mathscr C^\bullet\) is cohomologous to a smooth closed form. It also shows that a smooth form which is exact as a current is already exact in the de Rham complex. Consequently,
\[
H^q(\mathscr C^\bullet(M),d)
\cong H^q_{\mathrm{dR}}(M;\mathbb C).
\]

Thus passing from smooth forms to the larger current complex introduces no new cohomology classes; it only enlarges the space of representatives enough for the dynamical series to converge. The theorem therefore separates two phenomena:

- **topology**, encoded by de Rham cohomology and the action of \(f^*\) on it;
- **dynamics**, encoded by the expansion rate of \(f^*\) on exact currents.

A spectral gap between these rates canonically selects one invariant—or normalized invariant—current from each relevant de Rham class. A corresponding backward-iteration version holds when the gap is in the opposite direction, using \(f^{-1*}\).
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.output: We establish existence and uniqueness results for invariant currents and measures in smooth and holomorphic dynamical systems, with particular emphasis on noninvertible maps. Our approach formulates invariance through complexes of sheaves of differential forms and currents, whose hypercohomology is canonically identified with de Rham cohomology. This cohomological framework isolates the relevant invariant classes and, combined with analytic compactness and positivity arguments, yields canonical current representatives and associated invariant measures. The results apply to broad classes of smooth and holomorphic endomorphisms, extending methods that traditionally rely on invertibility and clarifying the cohomological origin of dynamical invariants.
